newsitem.title: GERMANY: German doctors protest drug payment cuts.
newsitem.headline: German doctors protest drug payment cuts.

text.p: More than 20,000 German private doctors closed their offices on Wednesday and took part in demonstrations around the nation to protest against pharmaceutical cutbacks ordered by the health ministry.

Staging rallies in small towns and cities between Munich and Berlin, the doctors denounced Health Minister Horst Seehofer's plans to cut health insurance reimbursement to physicians who prescribe drug treatments that exceed quotas.
Seehofer has threatened to charge doctors for the excess prescriptions, a move that the doctors said could cost some private physcians as much as 70,000 marks.
"That would spell doom for a lot of private practices," said Wolf-Ruediger Ruddat, a leader of the protest.
There were more than 4,000 physcians at one rally in the eastern city of Erfurt, while some 9,000 took part in the demonstrations across the southern state of Bavaria.
Seehofer has led a campaign to cut pharmaceutical costs in Germany with a healthcare reform law that took effect in 1993.
Among other measures, it forced pharmaceutical firms to cut selling prices by five percent and put upper limits on the amounts of drugs doctors could prescribe each year for their patients.
